simple.meaning: צַמּוּק (tsammûwq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a cake of dried grapes.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, beginning at 1 Samuel 25:18. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two containers of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs* 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks of parched grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on donkeys.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two containers of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs* 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks of parched grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on donkeys.
They gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his spirit came again to him; for he had eaten no bread, and drank no water for three days and three nights.

When David was a little past the top, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a couple of donkeys saddled, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a container of wine.
